payload.text:
The harness derives its population label from what actually ran, never from a flag someone passed, and refuses a verdict without one. GRADED IN THREE LEGS OF DIFFERENT QUALITY, because the row read as one claim and is not -- snorkeltoast's split, verified by vc at the source, and the row stays UNSATISFIED on the middle one. LEG 1, ARTIFACT-LEVEL POPULATION: DERIVED AND RAN. capture() writes artifact_sha256 and population_source into manifest.json and compare prints the POPULATION block, so what is graded is identified by what was actually photographed rather than by an assertion. LEG 2, PRODUCER-LEVEL POPULATION: A FLAGGED GUESS, AND THIS IS WHAT HOLDS THE ROW OPEN. The run's label reads "adjacency (UNVERIFIED)" because no artifact stamps its own builder, so the producer is inferred to be the compiler that sat BESIDE the harness at capture time. compare says so loudly and marks the verdict PROVISIONAL, which is the honest form and not the required one: THE ROW ASKS FOR A LABEL DERIVED FROM WHAT RAN, AND ADJACENCY IS NOT THAT. It is not a flag someone passed either, so the row is half-met rather than violated. LEG 3, THE REFUSAL: PRESENT, TERMINAL, AND NEVER FIRED -- and it is a SOUND detector zero rather than a tautology, which is the distinction this thread keeps having to make. Read at showreel-harness:1150, the first die in cmd_compare: "the {name} capture carries no artifact identity", reached before STRUCTURE and before everything else, ending in sys.exit(1). It cannot fire on a manifest capture() wrote, because capture() always writes the identity -- but a hand-edited or partially-written manifest is a real input class and the branch is reachable from it. So it COULD fire, which is what makes the zero worth something; contrast AC-2.17's UNDECIDED branch, which no input could reach. DISCHARGED WHEN LEG 2 BECOMES A DERIVATION, WHICH IS WP-03'S TO GIVE: once the Rust build stamps its own identity into the artifact, the producer stops being the thing that was standing nearby and becomes the thing that is recorded. This is a real WP-02-on-WP-03 dependency and is stated here so it is not rediscovered as a surprise.
"STAMPS ITS OWN IDENTITY" IS UNDERSPECIFIED AND THE HARNESS ALREADY SPECIFIES IT. Measured by vc 2026-09-09 20:17Z, before the stamp is written rather than after the one-shot compare is spent. `producer_stamp` reads `<meta name="showreel-producer" content="...">` (showreel-harness:226, STAMP_RE at :222). NOTHING ON EITHER SIDE WRITES IT: four greps -- the reference player.html, the reference compiler, the pulled template, the Rust src/ -- all zero, and the same instrument returned a real hit for `producer` at showreel:1006, so the zero is a sound detector zero rather than a tautology. THAT :1006 HIT IS ALSO THE TRAP: `"producer": cfg.get("producer", "")` is the REEL'S CREDIT LINE, a different thing under the same word, and the pulled template renders it as `add("Producer", REEL.producer)` -- so the artifact already carries "Producer" and a value in a sense that has nothing to do with who built it.
THE CONTENT IS SPECIFIED BY THE INSTRUMENT'S OWN COMMENT AND BY NO ROW (showreel-harness:218-223): an identifier covering the pixel-affecting rules -- long edge, resampling filter, quality, and the alpha rule -- "because once ST0017 C2 retires the alpha asymmetry, a Rust build over Python masters is a pipeline whose halves disagree about policy by construction, and `rust` alone cannot say that." SO A STAMP READING content="rust" MEETS THIS ROW'S LETTER AND DEFEATS THE INSTRUMENT: population_source flips to "stamp", leg 2 reads as derived, and the condition the derivation exists to detect stays invisible. A row satisfiable by machinery that does not do the job is the error this contract has already caught three times, and it is written down here so it is not committed a fourth.
THE FOUR RULES, MEASURED ON BOTH SIDES. Long edge master 2560 both (showreel:51, normalise.rs:34); long edge embed 1920 both (showreel:52, normalise.rs:37); filter Lanczos both (showreel:314 and :447, normalise.rs:175); JPEG quality 86 both (showreel:53, normalise.rs:41). THREE OF FOUR AGREE AND THE FOURTH IS THE DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE: the reference collapses opaque alpha in init and not in build, the port collapses in both -- design.md 4.2's ruling, and AC-3.4 is the row that carries it. So the alpha rule is the ONLY one of the four whose value distinguishes the halves, which is exactly why the comment names it and why an implementation name alone cannot serve.
SEQUENCING, AND IT IS WHY THIS IS RECORDED NOW RATHER THAN AT GRADING. The first `compare` against a Rust artifact happens exactly once. cc's stated payload list -- build_socials, build_bug, the slide rows, the limits block, the build verb -- does NOT include the stamp, so on today's plan that one-shot measurement is spent on an artifact still reading "adjacency (UNVERIFIED)" and this leg does not move. THE MECHANISM IS JSON-FREE AND BUILDABLE WHILE WP-03 IS BLOCKED: template.rs keeps MARKERS and subs as two deliberately separate lists, so a fifth marker is already guarded by `every_marker_is_filled_and_none_survives_into_the_artifact` and `the_shell_declares_each_marker_exactly_once`. Only the EMISSION needs the payload; the marker, the Filling field and the substitution do not.
THREE CORRECTIONS FROM snorkeltoast 2026-09-09 20:31Z, ALL MEASURED, AND TWO OF THEM ARE TO vc'S FIELD LIST ABOVE.
(1) THE TAG MUST SHIP AS A SUBSTITUTION TOKEN AND NEVER AS LITERAL TEXT, OR EVERY RUST ARTIFACT STAMPS ITSELF PYTHON. `showreel:1018-1022` builds the artifact as `PLAYER.read_text()` plus four `.replace()` calls, so THE ARTIFACT IS player.html WITH SUBSTITUTIONS -- and cc PULLS that template. A tag carrying a real value in the shared shell would be inherited verbatim by the Rust build, `producer_stamp()` would find it, and `population_source` would flip from "adjacency (UNVERIFIED)" to "stamp": AN HONEST REFUSAL UPGRADED INTO A CONFIDENT WRONG ANSWER, believed precisely because a stamp outranks adjacency. It is the compiler_adjacent failure again, one file wide, carried across the port boundary by the copy that makes the move a directory copy. **VERIFIED IN cc'S WORKING COPY BEFORE THIS WAS WRITTEN: player.html:7 is `content="__PRODUCER__"`, MARKERS is 5, and cc added two refusals vc did not specify -- an empty producer, and one carrying a quote that would break the tag.** So the hazard is absent in the port. THE RESIDUE IS snorkeltoast'S AND IS OWNED: an artifact whose stamp is still the literal token must REFUSE, not warn -- the case that arrives the day Python stamps and someone adds the tag without the substitution.
(2) `edge=2560` DOES NOT BELONG IN A BUILD STAMP. `MASTER_MAX` is an INIT constant (`showreel:51`, read by `normalise`) and the build half never reads it. Putting it in a build stamp is the STAGE-MIXING the field exists to prevent, and it is exactly the case in play: population (2) is a Rust build over Python masters, so the build stamp's author did not perform the init step the field would be describing.
(3) `embed=1920` MUST BE THE REEL'S ACTUAL TARGET, NOT `TARGET_DEFAULT`. `showreel:989` is `target = int(cfg.get("target", TARGET_DEFAULT))` -- per-reel overridable -- so a stamp reading 1920 on a reel carrying `target: 1440` is false on its face.
THE SHAPE, snorkeltoast's, AND THE RULE THAT GOVERNS IT: `impl=<name>/<version>;stage=build;embed=<actual target>;filter=lanczos3;q=<JPEG_Q>;alpha=<rule>`. VALUES, NOT A VERSIONED POLICY ID -- an id is an identifier standing in for the property it names, and it fails silently in the one case the stamp exists for, someone editing a constant without bumping the id, leaving two halves agreeing on `pixpol-3` and disagreeing on pixels. AND EVERY VALUE INTERPOLATED FROM THE LIVE CONSTANT, NEVER WRITTEN OUT: a hardcoded `q=86` is a flag wearing a stamp's clothes, recording what somebody intended when they typed it. That is showreel-harness:218's own distinction one level deeper.
THE ALPHA DIVERGENCE IS NARROWER THAN vc STATED AND THE CORRECTION IS snorkeltoast'S. vc wrote it as "the reference collapses in init and not in build". The two sites: init at `showreel:304-309` PROBES the channel and collapses fully-opaque RGBA to RGB; build at `showreel:449` tests `im.mode` ONLY. **IN A PYTHON-INIT-THEN-PYTHON-BUILD PIPELINE THE ASYMMETRY IS UNREACHABLE** -- init already collapsed the opaque case and wrote a .jpg, so build never meets an opaque RGBA. It becomes reachable exactly where build meets a master init did not write: hand-placed inputs, which `master_normalisation` already counts and names as OUTSIDE init's buckets. **A MIXED PIPELINE PLUS A HAND-PLACED OPAQUE-RGBA MASTER IS THE WHOLE OF THE DIVERGENCE** -- narrow, real, and currently invisible. Values `alpha=mode-only` and `alpha=collapse`, distinct strings, which is what makes it surface.
AND A HARNESS-SIDE CONSEQUENCE snorkeltoast OWNS: `producer_stamp()` returns the raw string, so two stamps that differ must report WHICH FIELD differs. A whole-string compare on a six-field string tells a reader that something moved and not what, and the answer is one parse away.
cc'S PRE-FLIGHT ON THE SIX FIELDS 2026-09-09 20:42Z: TWO CANNOT BE INTERPOLATED AS THE TREE STANDS, AND ONE OF THEM IS UNTESTABLE BY THIS ENTIRE ESTATE. Four are fine -- `impl` from `env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME")`/`env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` by construction, `q` from `normalise.rs:41`, and `stage`/`alpha` correctly literal because they are policy words naming which half wrote the stamp, which IS a constant fact about the writer.
`filter` CANNOT BE INTERPOLATED TODAY. `image::imageops::FilterType::Lanczos3` is INLINE at `normalise.rs:175`, at the resize call, with no named constant -- verified by vc at source. So `filter=lanczos3` in a stamp would be a hardcoded literal, which is the flag-wearing-a-stamp's-clothes failure one line after this row names it. It needs hoisting to a const that the resize and the stamp both read, and that has to land BEFORE any stamp content does.
`embed` HAS ITS VALUE PARSED AND NOTHING CARRIES IT TO THE EMBED SITE. `config.rs:173` is `pub target: Option<u32>` with a test asserting `Some(1920)`, so parsing is not the gap -- THREADING is. The reference runs `plan(reel, cfg, target)` at `showreel:553` into `embed(path, target, role)` at `:435`; cc's `plan()` takes no target at all. Nothing is wrong yet because nothing embeds yet; it is a live hazard for the payload slice.
AND THE ESTATE CANNOT CATCH THE DEFECT THIS CORRECTION IS ABOUT -- cc FOUND IT ON THE LIVE REEL AND vc MEASURED IT WORSE. 45h sets `target: 1920`, which is EXACTLY `normalise::TARGET` (`normalise.rs:37`). So a build that wrongly read the CONSTANT instead of the CONFIG emits byte-identical output, passes every test and grades green. **vc then checked the pinned fixture and it sets `target: 1920` TOO** -- so it is not "the one live reel", it is BOTH MEMBERS OF THE CONFIG POPULATION, including the fixture cc pinned under "test against something you did not write". The estate is blind to it by construction.
THIS IS THE ARGUMENT FOR THE CORRECTION AND NOT AGAINST IT, and it upgrades a note into a requirement: a stamp reading `embed=1920` off the constant is indistinguishable from one reading it off the config, everywhere in this estate, forever. **A FIXTURE CARRYING A NON-DEFAULT `target:` IS REQUIRED BEFORE THE `embed` FIELD CAN BE GRADED**, and unlike the `files:`/`exclude:` limits recorded on AC-3.2 this one is NOT a stated limit to live with -- there the missing coverage is of an input class nobody uses, here it is of the exact discrimination the field exists to make.
vc'S "REQUIREMENT" FRAMING ABOVE IS CORRECTED BY snorkeltoast 2026-09-09 20:48Z ON TWO COUNTS, AND THE SECOND ONE RECLASSIFIES IT.
(1) THE TWO MEMBERS ARE IN TWO DIFFERENT ESTATES AND vc COUNTED THEM AS ONE POPULATION. snorkeltoast's tree holds exactly ONE showreel.yaml -- the live 45h reel -- and no fixture reel at all; `bin/showreel` carries the compiler, the harness, player.html, themes and four docs. The pinned fixture vc checked is Utilz-side. So it is one member there and one member here, and NEITHER estate can vary `target` rather than one estate having two blind members.
(2) THE EMBED FIELD IS GRADEABLE TODAY WITHOUT ANY FIXTURE, BY A DIFFERENT INSTRUMENT. The artifact carries its slides as data URIs and their long edge is MEASURABLE -- decode and read the size -- so the stamp's `embed` claim can be graded against the pixels it claims to describe. **That is deriving from CONTENTS rather than comparing two self-reports**, it works on 45h as it stands, and it catches any builder whose stamp disagrees with what it actually embedded whatever the config says.
SO WHAT NOTHING HERE CAN PROVE IS ONE PATH, NOT ONE FIELD: that a builder reads the CONFIG rather than the CONSTANT. **AND ON THE ONLY CASE AVAILABLE -- the two being equal -- THAT PATH PRODUCES CORRECT OUTPUT.** There is no defect present to detect; the bug is LATENT, not manifest. A non-default-target fixture would not catch a wrong number on 45h, it would prove a code path is exercised at all.
**THAT MAKES THIS BLIND IN THE TAXONOMY RATHER THAN A GAP IN GRADING** -- a real difference, unobservable in this estate, which must be STATED EVERY RUN. It is the `shipped-max-ease` shape and it carries a genuine retirement condition: the day any reel sets a non-default `target` the estate can see, the row goes quiet by itself. The caveat is GUARDED to print only where `cfg.get("target", TARGET_DEFAULT)` equals `TARGET_DEFAULT`, because an unguarded caveat true on every reel today and false the moment a fixture exists is exactly what trains a reader to skip the line -- AC-4.1 records the same guard being added for the same reason.
AND THE FIXTURE IS NOT A CONFIG LINE, WHICH MATTERS BECAUSE IT SOUNDS LIKE ONE: a reel needs ASSETS to embed, so "a fixture with `target: 1440`" is adding images, not editing yaml, and must be costed as that if it is ever taken.
NEITHER PIECE IS BUILT TODAY AND THE REASON IS THIS CONTRACT'S OWN LESSON: no implementation emits the stamp yet, so a measured-embed check would be machinery whose subject does not exist and a port-expectation row would be one nothing can fire against. That is the shape vc's sweep found and snorkeltoast deleted at `cea163a` the same afternoon. Both are small once the stamp lands and both have a subject then.
THE FILTER HOIST IS A PREREQUISITE ON BOTH SIDES AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME DEFECT UNDERNEATH. snorkeltoast 2026-09-09 20:59Z, verified at source by vc. Three of the four pixel rules already have named owners in the reference -- `MASTER_MAX` showreel:51, `TARGET_DEFAULT` :52, `JPEG_Q` :53. **The fourth has none on EITHER side**, so a stamp reading `filter=lanczos3` records what somebody TYPED rather than what RAN: **the flag-versus-stamp distinction reappearing INSIDE the stamp**, the artefact built to record execution itself recording intent.
BUT THE TWO SIDES DIFFER IN KIND AND THE ROW SHOULD SAY SO. cc's is ONE inline site (`normalise.rs:175`) with no name -- a NAMING problem. **The reference's is TWO** -- `showreel:314` and `showreel:447` -- byte-identical `im = im.resize((round(w * s), round(h * s)), Image.LANCZOS)` lines with nothing binding them, which is a DUPLICATION problem and strictly worse. snorkeltoast's own opening ("mine is doubled") is the accurate reading; their later "the same defect in both implementations" understates their finding.
AND THE TWO SITES SIT ON THE SEAM THAT ALREADY DIVERGES, WHICH vc CONFIRMED BY FUNCTION RATHER THAN BY LINE. `normalise_image` (def :294) contains BOTH the alpha probe at :308 and the filter at :314; `data_uri` (def :440) contains BOTH the filter at :447 and the alpha test at :449. **So each of the two halves carries exactly one alpha statement and one filter statement, and the alpha pair is the known divergence** -- one probes the channel's extrema, the other reads only `im.mode`. Anyone repairing the alpha asymmetry edits both functions and can touch one resize and not the other, and nothing in the tree would report it.
NOT FIXED, AND THE REASONING IS THE ONE THIS ROW ALREADY RECORDS ONE PARAGRAPH UP. Both sites say LANCZOS today -- **latent, not manifest, no defect present to catch** -- and the cost runs the wrong way: `showreel` is the reference under active port, so editing it moves cc's target mid-port, and it is what builds the live reel days from the event. Later costs snorkeltoast one commit; now costs two other people something for a defect doing nothing. **It travels in the same commit as Python's own stamp, whenever hv's event window closes** -- and it is a PREREQUISITE of that stamp rather than a tidy-up, because a Python stamp landing without the hoist is a literal and the thread bought nothing on that side.
THE STAMP'S CONTENT LANDED AT 7512348 AND IT NARROWS THE BLINDNESS RECORDED ABOVE. Verified at source by vc 2026-09-09 21:06Z. `normalise.rs:54` is `pub const FILTER: image::imageops::FilterType = ...Lanczos3`, `:196` is the single `resize_exact(nw, nh, FILTER)`, and `filter_name()` at `:60` DERIVES the text as a Debug format lowercased rather than restating it -- so a variant rename fails to compile and a formatting change fails its pinning test.
cc CLOSED THE CONFIG-VERSUS-CONSTANT PATH STRUCTURALLY RATHER THAN BY TEST, WHICH IS BETTER THAN THE FIXTURE THIS ROW ASKED FOR. `stamp.rs:48` is `pub fn producer(cfg: &config::Reel)`, NOT a `u32`: a caller holding a number can pass `normalise::TARGET` by mistake and a caller holding the config cannot, with `Reel::embed_target()` (`config.rs:213`) the one home the payload slice will also read. AND IT IS EXERCISED AFTER ALL -- `stamp.rs:102-103` assert `embed=1440` and `embed=2560` from parsed config strings, so the reading path is covered at the unit level WITHOUT a fixture reel carrying assets.
SO THE BLIND SET SHRINKS AGAIN AND vc STATES WHAT SURVIVES: not that a builder reads the config rather than the constant -- that is now both unrepresentable and tested -- but the END-TO-END check that a real artifact's EMBEDDED PIXELS match the stamp's claim, which still waits on an artifact and on a reel with a non-default target. snorkeltoast's measured-embed instrument reaches it the day the stamp is emitted.
AND cc'S RED-PROOF CAUGHT A VACUOUS ASSERTION INSIDE THE TEST WRITTEN TO PREVENT ONE, WHICH IS THE MOST GENERAL FINDING ON THIS ROW. Injection: move `TARGET` 1920 to 1600, the stamp's `embed=` must follow. IT DID NOT FIRE. The assertion read the constant on BOTH sides, so moving it moved both and the test stayed green. One implementation agreeing with itself, written into the one test whose stated job is to stop exactly that, and the only assertion in the module that could not fail. Now a literal `embed=1920` (`stamp.rs:111`), and it fires; the vacuous form is recorded in the test's own comment at `:106` rather than silently replaced.
THE RULE, IN cc'S WORDS AND WORTH MORE THAN THE INSTANCE: THE VACUOUS FORM IS THE ONE THAT LOOKS MOST RIGOROUS. Writing the constant into the assertion looks like sourcing the value; typing `1920` looks lazy. It is the other way round. The other two injections fired first time -- `q=86` stops being true when `JPEG_Q` moves, `filter=lanczos3` when `FILTER` moves.
`stamp::producer` HAS NO CALLER AND cc PUT THAT ON THE RECORD RATHER THAN LEAVING IT TO A SWEEP. It joins the four pub fn vc measured as having no production reference, all of them build path. Leg 2 discharges when an artifact carries a FILLED stamp, not when the function exists.
